slides.texte_overlay:
strange truths about the human
mind most people never learn

the first impression trap

we judge people within seconds and then look for proof that we were right. knowing this helps you give people a fairer, kinder second chance before you decide.

the kindness loop

when someone does us a small favour, we feel pulled to return it. tiny kind gestures create far more goodwill than grand, impressive ones ever really do.

curious minds look warmer

we naturally see curious people as warmer and easier to trust, so learning a little each day changes how people respond to you. curiosity is one of the most attractive traits a person can have.
slides.texte_sophia:
curious minds look warmer

we see curious people as warmer. i spend 5 minutes a day on one lesson in the Sophia app, a planet or a painting, and people respond to me with so much more warmth now.

slides.texte_overlay:
familiar feels friendly

we tend to like things simply because we've seen them before. it's why people you see every day slowly feel friendlier, even without a real conversation.

nobody is watching that closely

people notice your small mistakes far less than you think. everyone is busy worrying about themselves, so you can relax a little and stop overthinking.
